Your Bones

Oxford Read and Discover · Level 2 · Your Body · Pages 6–7

🔒 New Words 1 · Listen & Fill 2 · Write 3 · Present 4 · Mind Map

★ New Words

🔒 This part is for the teacher.

Teach these words before the listening task. Press 🔊 to hear the word (American English). Show the picture, read the meaning, then read the example.

bone

noun

A hard, white part inside your body.

“There are bones under your skin.”

skeleton

noun

All the bones in your body together.

“These bones make your skeleton.”

joint

noun

A place where two bones meet.

“Elbows and knees are joints.”

elbow

noun

The joint in the middle of your arm.

“Elbows are joints.”

knee

noun

The joint in the middle of your leg.

“Knee joints help you to jump.”

kick

verb

To hit something with your foot.

“Knee joints help you to jump and kick.”

baby

noun

A very young child.

“A baby has small bones.”

skateboard

noun

A board with wheels. You stand on it and ride.

“When you ride a skateboard, wear pads.”

pad

noun

A soft thing you wear on your knees or elbows.

“Wear pads to protect your joints.”

helmet

noun

A hard hat. It keeps your head safe.

“Wear a helmet to protect your head.”

2 Write a Summary

Write about your bones in your own words. Write 15 words or more. Then you can see my example.

💡 Answer these questions

  1. Where are your bones?
  2. What do your bones make?
  3. What does your skeleton help you do?
  4. Where do bones meet?
  5. What do joints help you do?
  6. How can you protect your bones?

✏️ Start like this

  • My bones are under …
  • My bones make …
  • My skeleton helps me to …
  • Bones meet at …
  • Elbows and knees are …
  • When I ride a skateboard, I wear …
0 / 15 words

⭐ Example Summary

I have bones under my skin. My bones make my skeleton, and my skeleton helps me to stand up. Bones meet at joints. My elbows and knees are joints. Joints help me to move, jump, and kick. A baby has small bones, but bones grow and make us big and tall. When I ride a skateboard, I wear pads and a helmet to protect my bones and my head.

3 Presentation Script

Read the script. Practise it. Then present to your class!

Hello!Start

Good morning, everyone! My name is ________. Today I want to talk about my bones.

Look at this picture. These people are skeletons! Can you see the bones?

👉 Smile. Show the picture of the skeletons playing soccer.
Part 1Skeleton

First, there are bones under our skin. These bones make our skeleton.

Our skeleton helps us to stand up.

👉 Stand up tall when you say “stand up”.
Part 2Joints

There are joints in our skeleton, too. Bones meet at joints.

Elbows and knees are joints. Joints help us to move. Knee joints help us to jump and kick.

👉 Point to your elbow and your knee. Do a little jump!
Part 3Bones grow

A baby has small bones. Bones grow, and they make us big and tall.

👉 Show “small” with your hands, then “tall”.
Part 4Fun fact

Here is a fun fact! Our bones stop growing when we are about 20 years old. Then there are 206 bones in our body!

Question for you: How many bones are there? (Wait.) Yes, 206!

👉 Ask the class. Wait. Say “Great!”
Part 5Protect

How can we protect our bones? When we ride a skateboard, we wear pads to protect our bones and joints. We wear a helmet to protect our head, too.

👉 Show the skateboard picture. Point to the pads and the helmet.
The EndFinish

Remember: our bones help us to stand, move, and jump. Let’s protect our bones!

Thank you for listening! Do you have any questions?

👉 Smile and say “Thank you!”

🌟 Presentation Tips

  • Speak slowly and loudly.
  • Look at your friends, not only at the paper.
  • Point to the pictures when you talk.
  • Smile! 😊
